verses.text: All the people gathered together in the square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel to follow.
On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly of men, women, and everyone old enough to understand what they heard.
In the square in front of the Water Gate, he read from early morning until noon before the men, women, and everyone who could understand. All the people listened closely to the Book of the Law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform built for the occasion. To his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah. To his left stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book where everyone could see him, because he was standing above the crowd. As he opened it, everyone stood up.
Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people lifted their hands and answered, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the other Levites explained the law while the people stayed in their places.
They read clearly from the Book of God's Law and explained its meaning so the people could understand what they heard.

Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites teaching the people said, "Today is holy to the LORD your God. Don't mourn or weep." The people had all been weeping when they heard the words of the law.
Nehemiah told them, "Go and enjoy rich food and sweet drinks, and send some to anyone who has nothing prepared. Today is holy to our Lord. Don't grieve, because the joy of the LORD is your strength."
The Levites calmed the people, saying, "Be still. This day is holy. Don't grieve."
Then everyone went to eat, drink, share portions of their food, and celebrate, because they'd understood the words read to them.
On the second day the family heads of all the people, along with the priests and Levites, gathered with Ezra the scribe to study the words of the law.
They found that the LORD had commanded through Moses that the Israelites should live in temporary shelters during the festival in the seventh month.

They were to announce this throughout their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go into the hills and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees to build temporary shelters, as written."
The people went out and brought back branches. They made shelters on their roofs and in their courtyards, in the courtyards of God's house, and in the squares at the Water Gate and the Ephraim Gate.
Everyone who had returned from exile built temporary shelters and lived in them. The Israelites hadn't done this in that way since the days of Joshua son of Nun. There was great joy.
Every day, from the first to the last, Ezra read from the Book of God's Law. They celebrated the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly as prescribed.
